We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we gather (land on which we are broadcasting from) today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe and Chonnontan People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Rental Renovation and Tenant Support
notes: Report No.: COM2026-002
Prepared By: Grant Curlew

Grant Curlew gave a presentation outlining the rental renovation licensing report. He explored the options in front of Council today, including the tenant support liaison and a rental renovation licensing program. He then responded to questions of Council.

Jacquie Wells, Chair, ACORN Waterloo Region chapter and Ken Vogelpohl, Co-Chair, ACORN Waterloo Region chapter spoke about the work that ACORN has done, and spoke about their disappointment in the staff recommendations. They recommend the City implement a renoviction by-law with additional parameters. They then responded to questions of Council.
Grant Curlew responded to questions of Council. Nicole Papke and Ron Ormson also responded to questions of Council.

Alexandar Pavlov, Project Lead, Community Legal Information Project (CLIP) gave a presentation offering information on CLIP and the access to justice issue in the community. Alexandar Pavlov responded to questions of Council.
Council meeting recessed: (Time: 6:15 p.m.)
Council meeting reconvened: (Time: 6:31 p.m.)
Randall Withell, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the importance of a renoviction by- law, and how it would affect tenants in Waterloo.
Grant Curlew responded to questions of Council.

Elliot Wand, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the issues surrounding the N13s served on them and the other tenants in their building, as well as the need for more tenant protections. Elliot Wand also read a statement from another member of the community who was unable to register in time. Elliot Wand then responded to questions of Council.
Grant Curlew responded to questions of Council.

Ryan Murdock, Resident of Kitchener spoke against the staff recommendations and in favour of a strong renoviction by-law that includes temporary accommodations, rental top-ups, and moving costs. Ryan Murdock responded to questions of Council.
Kurtis Sutton, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the need for Waterloo to pass a renoviction by-law, and the poor conditions that some renters face.
Lynn Intini, Resident of Kitchener spoke about the poor conditions some renters face, and how landlords and investors need to be held accountable for bad actions.
Linda Vos, Resident of Kitchener spoke about the need to pass a strong renoviction by- law, and how bad faith renovictions affect tenants, especially those who are vulnerable.
Grant Curlew and Nicole Papke responded to questions of Council.
Councillor Wright having previously declared a pecuniary interest was absent for the taking of the vote.
Grant Curlew responded to questions of Council.
Following the failed vote, Councillor Vasic introduced an alternate motion.
Councillor Wright having previously declared a pecuniary interest was absent for the taking of the vote.

items.title: Questions
notes: Councillor Wright asked a question of staff regarding the lighting issue in Uptown, where there are a number of strobing lights. She asked if they could be removed until a replacement can be sourced. She asked staff if they could update her offline.
